reason: PairReplay maintains the explicit relation second=f(first) through default lookups, NOT/AND/OR moves, filtering and sorting. f0=0 and gate-homomorphism premises are explicit, so arbitrary malformed tags/records do not smuggle assumptions.

guarded transforms an actual child only after isPerm matches its first-coordinate list exactly. The relation and explicit run-preservation premise then transport that run to the second-coordinate list; mismatch returns the original list.
orbitLookup returns either one action applied to the original child or the untouched child. Its proof requires run preservation for every candidate action and does not trust the lookup result.

Binary search/sorting are deliberately untrusted hints: the soundness theorem permits any returned index, because the downstream indexed checker still checks bounds and exact isPerm. No sorted-table or search-completeness theorem is assumed.
The three kernel examples test specific binaryFind outputs only; they do not claim a universal search specification.
scope: Generic relation replay and run-preserving lookup hints, not complete concrete closure or the posted31-conjunct theorem.
